name: Sleeper stretch
summary: Lying on the affected side, elbow at 90°, gently press the forearm down toward the floor.
setup: Lie on the affected side, rolled very slightly back so you are on the outer edge of the shoulder blade — that pins it and is what keeps the stretch safe. Shoulder and elbow at 90°, forearm pointing up. With the other hand, press the forearm gently toward the floor until a stretch is felt behind the shoulder. Hold. Stop short of pinching.
why: The rotation happens toward the phone whichever way it is placed, and the pressure is applied by hand. Follow the guide and log the hold.
tempo: Ease in over 5 s, hold, release.
progression: Roll slightly forward (the modified version) if the front pinches.
contraindications: Pinching at the front of the shoulder — this stretch is not for everyone; a mild stretch behind the shoulder is the only target.

faults.label: Forcing the forearm down
faults.tip: A mild stretch behind the shoulder; pressing hard makes the joint guard.

faults.label: Shoulder blade not pinned
faults.tip: Lie slightly back onto the outer edge of the shoulder blade so it cannot slide. Without that the stretch pinches the front.

faults.label: Feeling it at the front
faults.tip: The stretch belongs behind the shoulder. Pinching at the front means stop and ask your physio.

faults.label: Rolling onto the back
faults.tip: Keep the shoulder blade pinned so the stretch stays in the capsule.

guide.surface: Firm floor with a pillow under the head.
guide.stop: Pinching at the front, or pain that lingers afterwards.
guide.cannotSee: The rotation and the hand pressure.

points.t: Directly under you, elbow bent 90°, forearm pressed gently toward the floor.
